{{Short description|Theorem that curves of bounded curvature contain a unit disk}}
{{Use list-defined references|date=February 2021}}
{{Use dmy dates|cs1-dates=ly|date=September 2026}}
[[File:Moon-in-puddle-green.svg|thumb|upright|A smooth simple closed curve of curvature at most one, and a unit disk enclosed by it]]
The '''Pestov–Ionin theorem''' in the [[differential geometry]] of [[plane curve]]s states that every [[simple closed curve]] of [[curvature]] at most one encloses a [[unit disk]]. It has also been called the '''moon in a puddle theorem'''.{{r|petzam}}

==History and generalizations==
Although a version of this was published for [[convex curve]]s by [[Wilhelm Blaschke]] in 1916,{{r|blaschke}} it is named for {{ill|German Gavrilovich Pestov|ru|Пестов, Герман Гаврилович}} and {{ill|Vladimir Kuzmich Ionin|ru|Ионин, Владимир Кузьмич}}, who published a version of this theorem in 1959 for non-convex [[smoothness|doubly differentiable]] {{nowrap|(<math>C^2</math>)}} curves, the curves for which the curvature is well-defined at every point.{{r|pesion}} The theorem has been generalized further, to curves of bounded average curvature (singly differentiable, and satisfying a [[Lipschitz continuity|Lipschitz condition]] on the derivative),{{r|acmv}} to curves of bounded convex curvature (each point of the curve touches a unit disk that, within some small neighborhood of the point, remains interior to the curve), {{r|aat}} and to curves whose curvature is bounded in a viscosity sense.{{r|lns}}

It does not generalize to higher dimensions: there exist surfaces whose [[principal curvature]]s are lower bounded by a constant, [[homeomorphism|topologically equivalent]] to embedded spheres, that do not contain a sphere with that constant curvature. One construction for this is based on the [[house with two rooms]], a topological complex that is [[contractible]] but not [[Collapse (topology)|collapsible]].{{r|petzam}}

==Applications==
The theorem has been applied in [[algorithm]]s for [[motion planning]]. In particular it has been used for finding [[Dubins path]]s, shortest routes for vehicles that can move only in a forwards direction and that can turn left or right with a bounded [[turning radius]].{{r|acmv|ablrsw}} It has also been used for planning the motion of the cutter in a milling machine for [[Milling (machining)|pocket machining]],{{r|aat}} and in reconstructing curves from scattered data points.{{r|guhtra}}
